# P08 — Ruth 3:1-5

## 1. Metadata
- **Pericope title:** Naomi's plan for rest; Ruth's total consent
- **BCV:** Ruth 3:1-5
- **Genre Group:** NARRATIVE
- **Genre:** HISTORICAL_NARRATIVE
- **Register:** INFORMAL_CASUAL

*(Versification note: Ruth's chapter and verse numbers are the same in English and Hebrew — no divergence in this pericope.)*

**Multi-level register tagging:**
The whole passage sits in INFORMAL_CASUAL. Both scenes shift to INTIMATE at scene level: the whole passage is a talk between Naomi and her daughter-in-law — Naomi's plan and Ruth's one-line answer. The narrator's voice frames only the speech-openings at v.1 and v.5.

## 2. Level 1 — Whole-Passage Movement

### 2.1 Prose Arc / Shape / Argument / Burden / Concern
The passage is one exchange between Naomi and Ruth. Naomi opens with a question that means she will seek it: my daughter, shall I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you? And now, she says, is not Boaz our kinsman, with whose young women you were? Tonight he is winnowing the barley at the threshing floor. Then the instructions, step by step: wash, anoint yourself, put your garments on you, and go down to the threshing floor; do not be known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking; when he lies down, know the place where he lies; go in, uncover the place of his feet, and lie down. The plan ends: he will tell you what you shall do. Ruth answers: all that you say I will do. What weighs on the passage is what the plan leaves open: after "lie down", Naomi says only that he will tell her what to do.

### 2.2 Context
Before this, Ruth gleaned with Boaz's young women until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest, and she lived with her mother-in-law (2:23). Naomi's word for rest here (manoach) is the rest-word of 1:9 (menuchah), when she wished that YHWH would grant each daughter-in-law rest, each in the house of her husband. At 2:20 Naomi told Ruth that the man is near to them, one of their redeemers; here she calls Boaz "our kinsman" (מֹדַעְתָּנוּ), a family word. Winnowing is the work at the threshing floor that separates the grain from the chaff; Naomi says Boaz is winnowing there tonight.

### 2.3 Emotion / Tone / Pace
Quiet and deliberate. Naomi's speech goes in small steady steps — a question, a name, a time and place, then instruction after instruction — each one plain, none explained. The pace is a single growing instruction; then the passage stops short on Ruth's one-line answer.

### 2.4 Communicative Function
This passage gives Naomi's plan: her question — shall I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you? — then Boaz, the night, the threshing floor and each step. It ends with Naomi's word that the man will tell Ruth what she shall do, and with Ruth's one-line answer: all that you say I will do. The rest-word of 1:9 comes again here.

## 3. Level 2 — Scenes / Episodes

### Scene 1 — The plan spoken (3:1–4)

**3A — Beings**

[[B3-Naomi]] — נָעֳמִי חֲמוֹתָהּ / Naomi her mother-in-law
- Role: the one who speaks — her question, Boaz, the night, the threshing floor, and every step
- Relationship: mother-in-law of [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth; widow of [[B2-Elimelech]] Elimelech; [[B13-Boaz]] Boaz is a kinsman of her husband (2:1)
- Referential form: the narrator gives both the name and the kinship-word together — "Naomi her mother-in-law"
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B9-Ruth]] — בִּתִּי / "my daughter"
- Role: the one Naomi asks "shall I not seek a resting place for you?"; the hearer of the instructions
- Relationship: Moabite daughter-in-law of [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi
- Referential form: "my daughter" in Naomi's words (3:1)
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז מֹדַעְתָּנוּ / "Boaz our kinsman"
- Role: the man Naomi names — our kinsman, winnowing the barley at the threshing floor tonight; the man Ruth is not to be known to until he has finished eating and drinking
- Relationship: of the clan of [[B2-Elimelech]] Elimelech (2:1); the owner of the field where Ruth gleaned until the end of the harvests (2:3, 2:23)
- Referential form: "Boaz our kinsman" (מֹדַעְתָּנוּ, a family word) at v.2; then only "the man" at v.3 and "he" at v.4
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B16-Young-Women]] — נַעֲרוֹתָיו / "his young women"
- Role: the workers Ruth was beside all season — the tie Naomi names between Ruth and Boaz
- Relationship: Boaz's female field-workers
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

[[PL6-Threshing-Floor]] — הַגֹּרֶן / the threshing floor
- Role: where the plan points — Boaz winnows there tonight; Ruth is to go down to it
- Type: the working-floor where grain is winnowed
- Effect on scene: the one place the plan names

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0014-Rest-Menucha]] — מָנוֹחַ / "a resting place"
- What it is: "a resting place" (manoach), a place of rest
- Function in scene: in Naomi's question — shall I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you?
- Cross-ref: the rest-word of 1:9 comes again (1:9 menuchah, 3:1 manoach); at 1:9 Naomi wished each daughter-in-law rest, "each in the house of her husband"

[[O2-Barley]] — הַשְּׂעֹרִים / the barley
- What it is: the harvested grain being winnowed
- Function in scene: what Boaz is winnowing at the threshing floor tonight

[[O13-Your-Garments]] — שִׂמְלֹתַיִךְ / "your garments"
- What it is: Ruth's outer clothing, put on after washing and anointing
- Function in scene: the third step: put your garments on you

[[CB_0042-Uncover-Feet-Margelot]] — מַרְגְּלֹתָיו / "the place of his feet"
- What it is: the place of his feet (margelot); the text says only that Naomi tells Ruth to uncover it
- Function in scene: the plan's last steps: go in, uncover the place of his feet, and lie down
- Cross-ref: the same word comes again later in the story

**3D — Times**
- None: the talk is not given a time; "tonight" is in Naomi's words — the night of the winnowing.

**3E — What Happens**
[[B3-Naomi]] Naomi her mother-in-law speaks to [[B9-Ruth]] her: my daughter, shall I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you? And now — is not [[B13-Boaz]] Boaz our kinsman, with whose young women you were? Behold, he is winnowing the barley at the [[PL6-Threshing-Floor]] threshing floor tonight. Wash, anoint yourself, put your garments on you, and go down to the floor. Do not be known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking. When he lies down, know the place where he lies; go in, uncover the place of his feet, and lie down. And he — he will tell you what you shall do.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Naomi asks Ruth: shall I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you? She names Boaz, our kinsman, winnowing the barley at the threshing floor tonight, and gives the steps: wash, anoint yourself, put your garments on you, and go down to the threshing floor; do not be known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking; when he lies down, know the place where he lies; go in, uncover the place of his feet, and lie down. She ends: he will tell you what you shall do.

**Significant Absence**
After "lie down" she says only: he will tell you what you shall do. The word redeemer (2:20) is not said here; Naomi calls Boaz "our kinsman".

### Scene 2 — The consent (3:5)

**3A — Beings**

[[B9-Ruth]] — וַתֹּאמֶר / "she said"
- Role: the one who answers: all that you say I will do
- Relationship: Moabite daughter-in-law of [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi
- Referential form: "she" (3:5)
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B3-Naomi]] — אֵלֶיהָ / "to her"
- Role: the one Ruth answers
- Relationship: mother-in-law of [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth
- Presence: PRESENT

**3B — Places**

- None: the text names no place in this scene.

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

None: no persistent objects in this scene.

**3D — Times**
- None: continuous with the talk of Scene 1.

**3E — What Happens**
[[B9-Ruth]] She says to her: all that you say I will do.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Ruth answers Naomi in one line: all that you say I will do.

**Significant Absence**
Ruth asks nothing; she answers in one line. The narrator does not say what she thinks or feels.
